business_scope.primary_industry_name: Manufacture of Marine Outboard Engines and Compact Generators

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Applicability depends on the investor's country of residence and ownership chain.
France–United States Income Tax Convention, as amended, where the investor is US tax resident.
France–China Agreement on the Encouragement and Reciprocal Protection of Investments, subject to its current scope and applicable EU-law constraints.
France–United Kingdom Convention for the Avoidance of Double Taxation, as amended, where the investor is UK tax resident.
France–Switzerland Convention for the Avoidance of Double Taxation, as amended, where the investor is Swiss tax resident.
France is also party to numerous bilateral income tax treaties and investment treaties; treaty entitlement requires beneficial ownership, residence, substance, and limitation-on-benefits analysis.
EU internal-market freedoms, EU customs law, EU sanctions law, and applicable EU trade agreements apply to the proposed French SAS.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: French Monetary and Financial Code, Articles L.561-1 to L.561-50, including Article L.561-2-2 defining the beneficial owner and Articles L.561-5, L.561-5-1, L.561-6, L.561-10 and L.561-15 concerning customer identification, beneficial-owner identification, enhanced due diligence, and suspicious transaction reporting. Implementing provisions are principally in Articles R.561-1 to R.561-22 of the Monetary and Financial Code. Beneficial-owner filing requirements for legal entities arise under the French Commercial Code, including Articles L.561-46 to L.561-50 and regulatory provisions in Articles R.561-55 to R.561-63. Corporate formalities are filed through the Registre National des Entreprises maintained by INPI under the French formalities regime. France implements EU AML Directives, EU Regulation 2015/847 on payer information, and applicable EU restrictive-measures legislation.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Identify and verify all direct and indirect beneficial owners, directors, authorized representatives, and controlling persons. Screen against UN Security Council lists, EU restrictive-measures lists, French national sanctions measures, and relevant domestic enforcement lists before incorporation and continuously thereafter. Screen for PEP, family member, and known close-associate status under Articles L.561-10 and R.561-18 to R.561-20 of the Monetary and Financial Code and apply enhanced due diligence and senior-management approval where required. OFAC screening is not generally mandatory for a purely French transaction without a US nexus, but is commercially prudent for US persons, US-dollar clearing, US-origin goods, or US financial institutions. Document adverse-media, source-of-wealth, source-of-funds, ownership-control, and rationale for risk classification. Report suspicions to TRACFIN where the reporting obligation applies.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: French INPI Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises, connected to the Registre National des Entreprises
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be stated in the incorporation documents and filing data. French company names may use Latin characters and may include lawful foreign-language terms, subject to French public-order, trademark, consumer-protection, and misleading-name restrictions. No general statutory requirement exists for a French-script version or mandatory transliteration. The name must not create confusion with an existing registered name, trademark, public authority, regulated profession, or protected designation. A separate trademark search with INPI and relevant EUIPO searches is required because company-name availability does not establish trademark clearance.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Words implying regulated financial, legal, public, educational, or professional status may require authorization or may be prohibited if misleading.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: France does not generally provide a standalone statutory company-name reservation with a universal 30-day validity period. A proposed SAS name is submitted as part of the incorporation formalities; any temporary blocking or filing workflow is procedural rather than a guaranteed statutory reservation. Before filing, conduct INPI trade-name, trademark, RCS, domain-name, and public-register searches. If INPI or the competent registry rejects or suspends the filing, obtain the written reason, correct the name or supporting evidence, and resubmit through the Guichet Unique. For a formal administrative decision, file an administrative claim with the issuing authority and, where appropriate, a recours gracieux or recours hiérarchique within the applicable deadline, followed by a judicial challenge before the competent administrative court. Registry disputes concerning commercial-registration decisions may require proceedings before the competent commercial court. Use French counsel to preserve deadlines and distinguish a registry refusal from a trademark or unfair-competition dispute.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: An SAS must have a registered office in France under the French Commercial Code. A domiciliation company or virtual office may be used if the domiciliation provider is legally authorized and the statutory requirements for the domiciliation contract, availability of correspondence, and disclosure of the registered address are satisfied. A virtual office is not adequate as the sole evidence of manufacturing substance for a marine-engine business. The company should maintain appropriate premises, production or assembly arrangements, technical files, product-compliance records, personnel or contracted operational capacity, accounting records, inventory controls, and management activity proportionate to the business. Manufacturing, import, customs, product-safety, environmental, labor, and tax authorities may require evidence of actual operations.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: No official fixed probability is published. For a newly incorporated SAS with no regulated-license application, the estimated annual probability of an unannounced physical inspection solely because of incorporation is low, approximately 1% to 5%. The combined probability of an inspection, audit, or documentary control by customs, tax, labor, market-surveillance, environmental, or product-safety authorities may reasonably be assessed at approximately 5% to 15% during the first operating years, increasing with imports, complaints, emissions issues, safety incidents, cash-intensive activity, unusual ownership, or high-risk jurisdictions. These are risk estimates, not statutory frequencies.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Articles L.210-1 to L.210-10 and L.227-1 to L.227-30 for the Société par Actions Simplifiée (SAS); Articles R.123-1 to R.123-31 on RCS registration; Décret n° 2023-227 on business formalities.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Commercial Court Registry) via the Guichet Unique des Formalités d'Entreprises operated by INPI.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Demande d'immatriculation au Registre National du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) — electronic formality using the standard business declaration (formulaire M0 / déclaration unique).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The SAS has no minimum statutory share capital; the capital must be freely fixed in the Articles and fully subscribed. Cash capital contributions must be deposited into a blocked company bank account or with the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations; the funds are released only upon issuance of the K-bis extract after RCS registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, unanimously by the shareholders of the Société par Actions Simplifiée, that: 1. The subscription of fifty thousand (50,000) ordinary shares by each signatory of the subscription sheet, at the nominal value stated in the Articles, is approved and credited. 2. The registered office is fixed at [address], in the jurisdiction of the Commercial Court of [city], and may be moved by the President subject to ratification. 3. [Name] is appointed President and [Name] is appointed Director General, each with full corporate powers; 4. The President is authorized to publish the legal notice, open bank accounts, and complete the RCS registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Infogreffe for name verification; bank or Caisse des Dépôts for capital blockage
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Verify the availability of the intended company name against INPI databases and RCS records. Draft the Articles of Association either as a notarized deed or as a private deed (sous seing privé). Open a blocked account in the future company name and deposit the cash share capital; obtain a capital deposit certificate from the depositary institution.
required_dossiers: Company name availability search report
Draft French Articles of Association (statuts)
Identity documents of all shareholders and officers
Certificate of no criminal or insolvency disqualification for the President
Bank certificate of capital deposit or blocked funds certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the company name is rejected, select and submit three alternate names. If the capital deposit certificate contains discrepancies, request a corrected certificate from the depositary bank before proceeding.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of Legal Notice of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Authorized legal announcement journal (Journal d'Annonces Légales) in the département of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Publish the mandatory legal notice containing the corporate name, legal form, registered office, share capital, corporate purpose, incorporation date, proposed duration, and names of officers. Obtain the attestation of publication from the legal announcement journal.
required_dossiers: Completed legal announcement text
Registered office address
Identity and appointment details of officers
Date of signature of the Articles
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If publication is delayed, contact the journal directly to arrange expedited publication. If material errors appear in the published notice, publish a corrective legal notice and file the correction with the Greffe.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Incorporation Dossier with Guichet Unique
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet Unique des Formalités d'Entreprises / Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the complete electronic incorporation dossier through the official portal formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr, using the standard enterprise formalities form. Include the signed Articles, legal notice publication attestation, capital deposit certificate, registered office occupation proof, and identity declarations for officers. The Greffe performs legal review and, upon validation, registers the company in the RCS and issues the K-bis extract.
required_dossiers: Signed Articles of Association
Attestation of publication in a legal notice journal
Bank or Caisse des Dépôts capital deposit certificate
Proof of enjoyment of the registered office (lease, domiciliation agreement, or ownership document)
Identity papers and LinkedIn-style declaration for all corporate officers
Potential economic ownership declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Greffe issues a formal query or observation, respond with corrected documents through the Guichet Unique within fifteen working days. Failure to cure within the deadline may require resubmitting the full formalities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce and INSEE (Institut National de la Statistique et des Études Économiques)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the RCS registration is validated, retrieve the official K-bis extract proving the legal existence of the SAS. Check that INSEE assigns a SIREN number and an APE code corresponding to French NAF classification 28.11Z, consistent with ISIC Rev. 4 code 2811.
required_dossiers: RCS registration acknowledgement
First K-bis extract
Declaration of principal activity for APE code alignment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the K-bis delivery is delayed or contains incorrect registered particulars, file a rectification demand with the Greffe and INSEE; a certified copy of the K-bis may also be obtained from the registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Social, Tax, and Governance Formalities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: URSSAF / Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE) / CARSAT / local Préfecture / Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company with the social security system and declare the President and employees where applicable. Open the corporate tax file with the competent tax office. Complete any mandatory governance instruments required by the Articles, and file environmental or site-specific declarations if the industrial premises fall within the ICPE regime.
required_dossiers: K-bis extract
List and identity documents of corporate officers
Bank account details of the company
Articles of Association and appointment minutes
Site plan and description of the industrial facility for ICPE thresholds
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If URSSAF or the tax administration requests additional supporting documents, provide the required information before the stated deadline. If the case is closed erroneously, file a request for reinstatement with supporting evidence and, where needed, request a tax residence certificate.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement (DREAL) under the Ministry of Ecological Transition, acting as the ICPE inspection and permitting authority.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: ICPE Environmental Operating Registration/Declaration — installation classée pour la protection de l'environnement applicable to the manufacturing, assembly, machinery testing, and surface treatment operations of the marine outboard engine facility.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de la Transition Écologique — Direction Générale de la Prévention des Risques / DREAL territorial directorate
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category III — Enregistrement (registration regime) under ICPE for metalworking, combustion engine testing, and incidental surface coating; a full EIA is not required below the upper thresholds set by Annex J of the French Environmental Code, but noise, emissions, and waste needs are assessed at registration.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater limits: pH 5.5-8.5; TSS < 60 mg/L; BOD5 < 50 mg/L; COD < 300 mg/L. Air emissions: process VOCs < 110 mgC/m3; diesel test-bench exhaust must meet UBA/European CO, NOx, and particulates limits; hazardous waste must be stored on impermeable surfaces and removed by an authorized carrier with chain-of-custody records.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification issued by the local fire and rescue service (SDIS), including installation control of extinguishing systems and evacuation routes; structural load design verification by an approved building control office; occupational risk assessment validated by CARSAT; annual workplace medical inspection by the occupational health service (aptitude photocard for workers dealing with oils, noise, and solvents).

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction générale des finances publiques (DGFiP), principally the relevant Service des impôts des entreprises (SIE); online tax procedures are administered through the DGFiP professional portal at impots.gouv.fr. Corporate formalities and business identifiers are processed through the national business formalities one-stop shop at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr, with registration data recorded in the Registre national des entreprises (RNE) and the national business register.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A French SAS formed in France completes its formation formalities through the national business formalities one-stop shop. Following registration, it receives a SIREN identifier and establishment-level SIRET identifier; the competent tax office assigns or confirms its tax accounts and VAT status. A French VAT identification number normally consists of the country prefix FR followed by a two-digit key and the SIREN. The company must register for professional access to the DGFiP portal and submit applicable corporate tax and VAT returns. A foreign business with taxable transactions in France must register with the competent DGFiP service for foreign businesses, the Service des impôts des entreprises étrangères (SIEE), or the competent SIE as applicable, and provide formation, identity, activity, representative, and transaction documents. A non-EU business may be required to appoint a French fiscal representative unless an applicable statutory exemption or mutual-assistance arrangement applies. EU businesses generally register directly without appointing a French fiscal representative. Registration and VAT reporting obligations can arise without a general turnover threshold for a non-established taxable person making transactions taxable in France.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A French SAS is ordinarily subject to French corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés, IS). Eligible SAS companies may elect temporary taxation under the personal income tax (impôt sur le revenu, IR) regime for up to five fiscal years, subject to statutory conditions, including limits on age, workforce, turnover or balance-sheet size, ownership, and the proportion of voting rights held by individuals and qualifying managers. The election is not a US-style check-the-box election and is unavailable where the eligibility conditions are not met. No general French election permits a SAS to elect transparent treatment solely by selecting a tax classification. French rules implementing EU anti-hybrid-mismatch provisions may deny deductions or require income inclusion in defined cross-border arrangements; they do not constitute a general entity-classification election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT; taxe sur la valeur ajoutée, TVA).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general turnover threshold applies to a French-established business conducting ordinary taxable activities: VAT registration and compliance are generally required from commencement of taxable activity, subject to the small-business franchise en base de TVA and other specific exemptions. The mainland-France franchise thresholds generally applicable to domestic small businesses are EUR 85,000 for sales of goods and similar activities and EUR 37,500 for services, subject to statutory qualification rules, prior-year/current-year tests, and legislative changes. These domestic franchise thresholds do not generally relieve a non-established supplier of French VAT registration where it makes transactions for which it is liable to account for French VAT. Separate EU cross-border small-enterprise rules and transaction-specific exemptions may apply.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France is introducing domestic business-to-business electronic invoicing and electronic transaction-data reporting in phases. Under the legislated timetable, all in-scope businesses must be able to receive electronic invoices from 1 September 2026; issuance obligations begin on that date for large and intermediate-sized enterprises and on 1 September 2027 for SMEs and micro-enterprises. In-scope invoices must use compliant structured electronic formats and be transmitted through the public invoicing portal or an approved private platform connected to the national system. The regime is not a universal real-time pre-clearance or digital-stamping system. Applicable transaction-data and payment data reporting requirements depend on transaction type and taxpayer category. Public-sector invoices are submitted through Chorus Pro. Cross-border transactions and specified transactions outside the domestic e-invoicing scope may remain subject to electronic reporting rather than domestic e-invoice issuance.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods dispatched or transported from France to a destination outside the European Union may qualify for VAT exemption with a right to deduct input VAT, provided the statutory conditions are met and the supplier retains evidence that the goods actually left the EU. Intra-EU supplies of goods may qualify for exemption only when the substantive conditions are satisfied, including transport to another Member State, a valid customer VAT identification number, and required reporting. Services are not automatically zero-rated because the customer or supplier is offshore: place-of-supply rules determine whether French VAT applies. Many B2B services supplied to a taxable person established outside France are outside the scope of French VAT, subject to exceptions; services taxable in France remain subject to the applicable French VAT treatment. A VAT credit refund is subject to the applicable return, evidence, and refund procedures.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Export customs declaration and export-result confirmation, including the MRN and exit confirmation where available
Commercial invoice, order or contract, and records identifying the goods, buyer, and transaction
Transport evidence appropriate to the route, such as bill of lading, CMR, air waybill, carrier confirmation, or delivery evidence
Proof of payment or accounting records supporting the transaction; an inward remittance certificate is not a general French statutory export-VAT document
For intra-EU exempt supplies, the customer's valid VAT identification number, transport evidence, and required EC Sales List reporting
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: France imposes no general statutory foreign-exchange repatriation deadline for export proceeds. A zero-rating or exemption claim unsupported by evidence of export or by the applicable transaction conditions may be denied, with output VAT assessed retrospectively, interest for late payment, and applicable tax penalties. Penalties depend on the nature of the error, disclosure, and conduct; deliberate fraud or fraudulent documentation can attract enhanced tax penalties and, where statutory elements are met, criminal sanctions. Input VAT refunds may be adjusted or recovered if the underlying entitlement is not established. The taxpayer should retain contemporaneous customs, transport, invoice, accounting, and payment evidence for the applicable French tax-record retention period.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Central Bank) in coordination with the Directorate General of the Treasury (DG Trésor) for balance-of-payments and direct investment reporting.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France fully liberalised current and capital account transactions under EU law. The euro is freely convertible; no general quantitative limits apply to profit remittances, dividend distributions, or capital repatriation to non-EU shareholders. Foreign investors may transfer funds in and out without exchange control authorisation. The only mandatory requirements are documentary reporting to Banque de France for cross-border financial flows above statutory thresholds, compliance with international sanctions, anti-money laundering rules, and the absence of any embargoed counterparty. Capital account transactions are likewise unrestricted but must be reported for statistical purposes on the French balance-of-payments (échanges extérieurs).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no mandatory surrender or conversion of export proceeds in France. Exporters may freely retain export receivables in authorised foreign-currency accounts (comptes en devises) or in euro-denominated accounts. No statutory timeline for conversion exists, and no minimum conversion ratio applies. Cross-border export payments must be included in the enterprise's monthly balance-of-payments declaration to Banque de France when aggregated transaction volumes exceed the regulatory reporting threshold.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (compte séquestre) and Operational EUR/USD Current Account with SWIFT/LC access
Operational EUR/USD Current Account plus Trade Finance and Documentary Credits facilities
Specialised Large-Corporate Clearing Account and Export Trade Settlement Services

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility is medium-high for a non-deposit operating account, but legally constrained. An EU/EEA-authorised e-money institution (EMI) may passport into France under ACPR notification and provide payment accounts, e-money issuance, and often SWIFT MT103 routing. However, an EMI cannot offer escrow, credit, or deposit facilities, and most cross-border digital EMIs lack direct French IBAN and TARGET2 access. For marine-engine trade settlements and documentary LC operations, a licensed credit institution remains mandatory. EMIs are therefore acceptable only for low-volume ancillary disbursements, not for capital escrow or trade clearing.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: At least one authorised natural person, typically a director, must be physically present at the bank or at a notary/representative for the corporate KYC interview unless a certified French video-identification process (PVID) is accepted by the institution. Full board appearance is not legally required; an individual may appear with a duly signed corporate power (mandat) and extract Kbis evidencing authority. In practice, most Tier-1 French banks still require a physical branch visit or the appointment of an established local corporate services agent for remote companies to complete onboarding.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque beneficial ownership chain with non-French and non-EU intermediate holding companies.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Group structure organigramme; certified copies of certificates of incorporation and bylaws for each holding entity; French Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs filing proof; passports of all individuals holding 25% or more; board resolutions of the French SAS and intermediate parent companies; sworn corporate statement confirming ultimate beneficial owners.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Prior bankruptcy, adverse judicial history, or registration as a Banque de France payment-incident or Fichier Central des Chèques (FCC) hit.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificat de non-inscription au registre des incidents de paiement; official French bankruptcy court search result; European judicial rehabilitation extracts; statement of source of funds; personal and corporate bank references; tax compliance certificates; reconstruction and business continuity narrative.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Forecast of high cross-border fund flows with non-resident related parties for capital expenditure funding.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Equity injection and intra-group loan agreements executed; French VAT registration certificate and SIREN/SIRET code; pro-forma invoices and purchase orders for marine outboard engine manufacturing equipment; customs declarations; audited proof-of-funds statements from the transferring bank; rationale documented for the absence of French financing.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity and shareholder loans must be received through licensed banks via SWIFT MT103 or, for euro transfers from EU member states, via SEPA Transfer with the mandatory ISO purpose code and detailed remittance narrative. The standard classification is 'capital increase / equity contribution' using SWIFT field 70 with the IBAN of the French operating account and corresponding supporting file: deed of incorporation or shareholders resolution, funds-availability evidence, and Banque de France balance-of-payments declaration. All receipts in excess of regulatory thresholds must be notified to DG Trésor monthly using the French external-financial-reporting process.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements for imported components and engine parts run through cleared bank-dependent rails: SWIFT MT103 for telegraphic transfer suppliers, and Commercial Letters of Credit issued through MT700 for higher-value or documentary supply contracts. Euro disbursements to EU beneficiaries rely on SEPA Credit Transfers; high-value euro payments use TARGET2 settlement across participating French banks. Documentation for outbound flows must include buyer-seller contract, pro-forma invoice, Bill of Lading, packing list, certificate of origin and, when required, EUR1 movement certificate, aligning disbursement with Incoterms and the underlying marine-engine manufacturing purchase order.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Non-Deliverable Forwards (EUR as reference currency only, where a deliverable alternative is unavailable)
Exchange-traded FX Futures on Euronext Paris

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements and statutory reports (Comptes annuels, Rapport de gestion, and Commissaire aux Comptes report when applicable) filed in the RCS file
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce – Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés, lodged via the INPI Guichet Unique
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary rule: shareholder approval within six months after fiscal year-end; deposit with the Greffe within one month after such approval. For a 31 December fiscal close, final filing generally falls by the end of July of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing activates a registry formal notice (mise en demeure); if uncured for 30 days, the public prosecutor may request judicial strike-off (radiation) from the RCS. The legal entity may be fined up to EUR 7,500 and managing officers up to EUR 1,500, and the president of the commercial court may order coercive daily penalties (astreinte).

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax and results declaration (Déclaration de résultats – IS, Cerfa 2065-SD with annexes)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) – Service des Impôts des Entreprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Calendar rule: for a fiscal year ended 31 December, due by 3 May of the following year. For a non-calendar fiscal year-end, due no later than the third day of the month following the expiry of four months after the closing date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers a penalty of 5% of assessed tax after expiry, increasing by 0.9% per completed month, plus late-payment interest (intérêt de retard). Habitual non-filing may cause automatic assessment under CGI Article 1687 and criminal fines against the managing director.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Updated beneficial-owner declaration (Déclaration des Bénéficiaires Effectifs) maintained in the RCS file
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce / RCS, lodged via the INPI Guichet Unique
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Event-driven: no annual filing is due if there is no change in ownership. If a share transfer changes beneficial ownership, the updated declaration must be filed within 15 calendar days after registration of the transfer.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Omission or late filing within 15 days may expose the company to an administrative fine up to EUR 7,500 and responsible natural persons to fines up to EUR 3,750; aggravated non-compliance can also support RCS strike-off proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual statutory-register audit evidence package (share register, minutes and decisions book, securities-movement ledger, UBO verification)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company registered office; available for inspection by shareholders, statutory auditor, judicial authorities, and DGFiP inspectors upon demand
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: At each fiscal year-end, reconcile all statutory registers before the annual accounts are approved; there is no external fixed filing date, but the package must be completed before the annual accounts deposit.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Defective or missing statutory books can lead to commercial-court sanctions, civil liability of directors, and fines under the Code de commerce; such records may also be rendered inadmissible in tax and litigation proceedings.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Appointment of a statutory auditor (Commissaire aux Comptes) is mandatory if an SAS exceeds at least two of three thresholds at the end of a fiscal year: balance-sheet total greater than EUR 4,000,000; net turnover exclusive of tax greater than EUR 8,000,000; average number of employees greater than 50 (Code de commerce, Article L823-1). Mandatory audit may also be required for parent companies of controlled subsidiaries or upon shareholder or judicial request.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP (Plan Comptable Général) applies to individual statutory annual accounts under Code de commerce Articles L123-12 et seq. and ANC regulations; consolidated accounts of groups satisfying EU thresholds use IFRS as adopted in the European Union.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: France does not require an automatic annual UBO re-declaration absent a change. The SAS must keep the RCS-filed beneficial-owner statement current and file an updated declaration within 15 days of any registered share transfer or other beneficial-ownership change. As annual internal discipline, the registered agent must reconcile the RCS-filed UBO sheet with the securities-movement register and either confirm continuity or file the updated declaration within the statutory 15-day window.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Shareholders / Securities Movements (Registre des Mouvements de Titres)
Register of Corporate Decisions and Minutes (Registre des Procès-Verbaux)
Register of Directors and Corporate Officers (Registre des Dirigeants)
Minute Book of Shareholder and Board Meetings

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 500 – USD 2,200 per year for registered office domiciliation in France; add USD 600 – USD 1,500 per year for professional registered agent and corporate secretarial maintenance. Paris-area or premium commercial domiciliation services are at the higher end.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 6,000 – USD 16,000 per audit cycle for a typical mid-size marine outboard-engine manufacturing SAS, depending on turnover, inventory complexity, intercompany transactions, and whether consolidated accounts are required.

stage_6.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory tax holidays or preferential deductions
